answer: Each agent may submit jobs freely, but payment is released only after a randomly selected human reviewer confirms the result, and reviewers earn fees from a bond that is slashed when audits reveal collusion. A sparrow can create many accounts, yet those accounts cannot cheaply manufacture independent, accepted work: the attacker must lock capital in bonds, pay for real review, and risk losing the stake. A raven coordinating a cluster faces the same audit risk at every vertex, so multiplying identities raises both operating cost and the chance of a costly penalty.
